messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert — p99 tail latency for /v1/stream in us-east-1 at 5.2s (SLO 1.5s). Time-to-first-chunk increased, client-side stalls observed. Error rate up ~0.9%. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/streams?panel=tail
amelia_oncall: acked. I'm on it. paging oncall-sre and eng-runtime. any immediate customer pages?
jordan_support: getting 5 active tickets referencing long stall/partial responses. two mention websocket disconnects. linking ticket IDs in thread.
leo_eng_runtime: seeing increased queue depth on streaming-proxy pods. continuous batching backlog spikes around 03:12 UTC. stack across proxy->runtime handoff shows slow write()s.
raphael_sre: can you paste the top error samples/logs? also check upstream kube events and node CPU/IO.
leo_eng_runtime: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T03:11:57Z proxy-abc write timeout to client fd=122: wrote 0 of 16384
2026-03-15T03:12:03Z runtime-1 kvcache miss, retrying
2026-03-15T03:12:07Z proxy-abc backpressure applied, queue=7342
```
amelia_oncall: thanks. quick checks: 1) Are proxies overloaded? 2) Is this a client slow-consumer problem? 3) Any recent deploys to proxy/runtime?
leo_eng_runtime: no deploys in last 6h. proxies at 85% CPU, epoll wait spikes on a subset of nodes. downstream model hosts OK.
ryan_ops: checking node metrics; EBS IOPS for a couple nodes in the autoscaling group spiked, causing syscalls to stall. bouncing two affected nodes.
simone_product: any customer-facing impact? need summary for comms.
jordan_support: two enterprise customers saw truncated streams and reconnect loops for ~12-20m. most sessions recovered. total of ~37k affected stream sessions (est.)
amelia_oncall: mitigation plan: (A) remove the two flaky nodes from LB (ryan) (B) temporarily lower proxy buffering thresholds to force earlier chunk flush (leo) (C) enable fallback routing to dedicated proxy group with spare headroom (raphael)
leo_eng_runtime: bumping buffer config now. applying config via k8s configmap:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  proxy.max_buffer_bytes: "8192"
  proxy.write_timeout_ms: "2500"
```
kubectl apply -f proxy-configmap.yaml -n streaming
```
leo_eng_runtime: rolling restart proxies with new config (one-by-one)
ryan_ops: cordoned nodes are draining. restarting kubelet on node-7 and node-9 now.
amelia_oncall: engines, watch p95/p99 and time-to-first-chunk on dashboard. raphael, prepare fallback route.
raphael_sre: fallback routing activated at 03:19 UTC — diverting 18% of stream traffic to proxy-dedicated-2 cluster.
leo_eng_runtime: after config and fallback, p99 dropped to 2.1s within 4m. errors decreased. still seeing a small tail at 1.9-2.5s for certain clients.
jordan_support: tickets updated. sent interim note to affected customers: "we are mitigating elevated streaming latency; partial reconnects possible."
simone_product: good. let's prepare post-incident comms once stable.
amelia_oncall: monitoring window now. we need to verify root cause: node I/O causing syscalls to stall -> backlog at proxy layer -> client backpressure -> stalled chunks.
leo_eng_runtime: hypothesis: large keepalive/slow-consumer connections allowed huge per-connection buffers, amplifying EBS/IO pressure. temporary config change limited buffer size which reduced amplification.
ryan_ops: node reboots completed; nodes back in service and healthy by 03:28 UTC.
raphael_sre: recommending follow-ups: 1) permanent proxy config change to lower max_buffer_bytes for streaming endpoints 2) add alert for epoll wait spike and EBS IOPS tail 3) run a soak test with slow-consumer simulator
amelia_oncall: moving to mitigation-complete state at 03:36 UTC. p99 stabilized ~1.4s (within SLO). marking incident as resolved-for-now but keeping page open for postmortem.
leo_eng_runtime: quick note — we also increased per-proxy connection limit and enabled earlier flush of partial chunks; stash change in repo: `git rev 9f3b1c`.
jordan_support: customers notified. three enterprise customers requested incident calls; calendar invites going out.
simone_product: tracking impact numbers for postmortem: ~37k sessions impacted, peak error rate +0.9%, median additional latency +0.8s, max observed p99 5.2s, affected window ~03:11-03:34 UTC.
amelia_oncall: handoff to night oncall @maya_oncall_next at 03:40 UTC. Maya — summary: elevated streaming tail latency due to node-level IO stalls causing proxy backpressure. Mitigations applied: cordoned nodes, proxy config limit, fallback routing, rolling restart. Alerts tuned. Actions left: validate config in canary, create postmortem, run slow-consumer load test, tune alert thresholds. Ownership: leo_eng_runtime (root cause triage), raphael_sre (alerting + routing follow-up), ryan_ops (node repro and I/O review), simone_product (customer comms)
maya_oncall_next: ack. I'll take it from here and keep eyes on the graphs. will ping if any regressions. thanks team. :raised_hands:
amelia_oncall: thanks all. adding task checklist in incident board and linking this thread to the incident ticket.
